subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing - FinLytics
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.in>
To: Sarah Johnson <sarah.johnson@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.in>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.in>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing - FinLytics

Sarah — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can size Dedicated correctly. Attaching the workload report you shared (FinLytics_ML_workload_report.pdf).

Call recap (high level):
- Primary workload: real-time customer-facing assistant + nightly bulk embedding jobs.
- Real-time: average ~10 RPS (requests/sec), peak ~30 RPS during business hours; avg concurrency ~6-8.
- Typical request token mix (approx): 25% short (<32 tokens), 50% mid (32-512 tokens), 25% long (>512 tokens). Typical input ~150 tokens, avg output ~350 tokens.
- Latency targets: p95 ~250ms for short prompts, p95 ~600ms for long/context-heavy prompts.
- Preferred model family: 16k context-capable LLMs (we discussed ~Redwood-verified 16k baseline).
- Compliance: SOC2 + data residency preference (US).
- Deployment preference stated on call: likely Dedicated initially, then evaluate Private VPC later.

Questions / clarifications we need to size:
1) Can you confirm peak RPS and concurrency (avg vs burst)?
2) For the nightly embedding jobs, do you expect those to run concurrently with real-time traffic or in a separate maintenance window?
3) Any hard constraints on GPU type? (H100 vs A100; H100 gives better perf for 16k context / larger KV caches but at a higher hourly rate).
4) Do you have a preferred SLA/availability target (99.9% vs 99.95+) or is latency the primary SLO?

Next steps I propose:
- If you confirm the numbers above, we'll run a quick capacity-sizing recommendation (target pool size + GPU type + concurrency config) and share a 30-day pilot plan.
- Schedule a 60m sizing workshop with your infra + our solutions engineer (Marissa) — she’s CC'd.
- I'll prepare a preliminary quote for Dedicated (ballpark) to share with procurement.

Thanks — if you can reply with the clarifications above I'll get the sizing calc started.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Exec — Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.in

Attachments: FinLytics_ML_workload_report.pdf

From: Sarah Johnson <sarah.johnson@finlytics.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.in>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.in>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.in>
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing - FinLytics

Thanks, Rafael — great recap. A few clarifications inline.

> Primary workload: real-time customer-facing assistant + nightly bulk embedding jobs.
Yes — exactly. Nightly jobs run on a maintenance schedule (midnight-03:00 PT) and we prefer them to be isolated from the real-time pool if possible.

> Real-time: average ~10 RPS (requests/sec), peak ~30 RPS during business hours; avg concurrency ~6-8.
Correction: average is closer to 12 RPS; peak is usually around 25 RPS for interactive flows. Concurrency hovers around 8 – but we do have spike events that push up to ~14 for ~1-2 minutes (during promotions).

> Token mix
We expect slightly heavier long-tail usage than you noted — long prompts are ~30% of requests due to transcript summaries.

> GPU preference
We’re agnostic but would like a recommendation. Our infra lead (Tom Hsu) will chime in with memory/context needs; we prefer lower cost if latency SLOs are met.

> SLA
Latency is primary; availability target 99.9% is fine for now.

Can you include a ballpark monthly committed capacity (and price) for a pilot (4-6 weeks) so procurement has something to review?

Thanks — Sarah
Sarah Johnson
Head of Product — FinLytics
sarah.johnson@finlytics.com

From: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@finlytics.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.in>, Sarah Johnson <sarah.johnson@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.in>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.in>
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing - FinLytics

Adding some infra detail from our side — forwarding sample telemetry and a small inference trace (finlytics-inference-sample.json).

- Real-time product uses a 16k-context model for session summarization; KV cache per session is non-trivial (~1.2GB per active session for our average prompt lengths).
- Typical concurrent active sessions: 6-10 under normal loads; promotional spikes (marketing) have pushed us to ~18 concurrent sessions for short bursts (~1-3 minutes).
- Nightly embeddings are batch jobs that we can schedule to avoid overlap with business-hours peak traffic; we prefer to run them in a separate cluster if feasible.
- For pilot sizing: we would like to validate steady-state throughput at p95 latency targets and also run a 30m promotion-stress test to validate autoscaling behavior.

Happy to join the sizing workshop — my availability next week is Tue/Wed morning PT.

—Tom
Tom Hsu
CTO — FinLytics

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.in>
To: Sarah Johnson <sarah.johnson@finlytics.com>, Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.in>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.in>
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing - FinLytics

Thanks for the quick clarifications — super helpful. Based on what you shared, here's our recommended starting config and next steps. I’ve attached a preliminary quote (redwood-dedicated-quote-v1.pdf) and a DocuSign link for the pilot commitment.

Recommendation (pilot):
- Deployment mode: Dedicated (separate cluster for real-time; optional separate cluster for nightly embeddings).
- GPU type: H100 80GB preferred for 16k-context models + KV cache memory headroom. A100 40GB is an option but would require more nodes and may increase p95 latency for long-context prompts.
- Initial pool: 4 x H100 (80GB) dedicated VMs. Rationale: supports steady-state ~20-25 RPS with room for 8-12 concurrent sessions and allows a 30m promotion-stress test to validate autoscale.
- Autoscaling: aggressive burst policy up to +50% for short bursts (1-3 minutes) — we’ll configure ephemeral capacity to handle the 18-concurrent spike you mentioned.
- Expected performance: p95 short prompts <250ms; p95 long prompts ~450-650ms depending on prompt length (we’ll hard-validate during pilot).
- Pilot length & goals: 4-6 weeks; validate p95 latency SLOs, throughput, and autoscale behavior; finalize committed pool size for production.

Ballpark pricing for pilot (monthly committed): $XX,XXX/month for 4 x H100 dedicated pool + managed infra and 24/7 support (detailed line items in attached quote).

Next steps:
- Please confirm you’re okay to proceed with Dedicated pilot and we’ll send a formal SOW + DocuSign for the pilot commit.
- Schedule a 60m capacity-sizing workshop (Marissa to lead) — proposed times: Tue 24 Mar 09:00 PT or Wed 25 Mar 10:30 PT. Tom — can you confirm Tue/Wed availability?
- Once SOW is signed we’ll provision a staging pool and run a 2-day smoke test before the formal pilot window.

If that all looks good I’ll route the DocuSign and set the workshop invite.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Exec — Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.in

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-quote-v1.pdf
